title: Manipuri Film ‘Enoong Ngallamdai (Fireflies in the Dark)’ Selected for Kolkata International Film Festival 2026
summary: Manipuri feature film Enoong Ngallamdai (Fireflies in the Dark), directed by Yogesh Lohan, has been selected for the official programme of Kolkata International Film Festival 2026.
body:
Imphal, November 24, 2026: Manipuri feature film Enoong Ngallamdai (Fireflies in the Dark) has been selected for the official programme of the Kolkata International Film Festival (KIFF) 2026, bringing another recognition to Manipuri cinema on a wider festival platform.

Directed by Yogesh Lohan, the 85-minute Manipuri-language film explores the human impact of the ethnic conflict that erupted in Manipur in 2023. Through three interconnected stories of survival, displacement and resilience, the film portrays the experiences of ordinary people caught amid violence and uncertainty.

The film follows three different narratives: a pregnant woman struggling to give birth while gunfire surrounds her, a young boy searching for his mother with a displaced calf accompanying him, and a café owner who risks her own safety to shelter people fleeing the violence.

**Stories of Survival and Humanity**

Written by Chingsanglakpa and Yogesh Lohan, the film adopts a non-linear storytelling approach to present the lives and experiences of people affected by the conflict.

Before developing the screenplay, director Yogesh Lohan travelled to Manipur and met survivors, drawing on their experiences to shape the story.

Explaining the intention behind the film, Lohan said he wanted to look beyond headlines about violence and displacement and bring attention to the fears, dignity and survival instincts of ordinary people.

The film was produced by Jani Viswanath and shot at actual locations across Manipur with the support of local communities. According to the production team, the film seeks to portray the human consequences of conflict without sensationalising violence.

Viswanath described the filmmaking experience in Manipur as deeply human, saying that the stories and resilience of the people encountered during production shaped the process. She said the film aims to highlight the futility of conflict and its impact on innocent lives.

**World Premiere at Vancouver International Film Festival**

Enoong Ngallamdai (Fireflies in the Dark) previously had its world premiere on October 6, 2026, at the Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF), where it was screened in the Panorama Cinemas of Asia section.

Its selection for KIFF 2026 marks another important festival platform for the Manipuri-language feature. The film was also featured in the WAVES Film Bazaar 2025 viewing room catalogue as a Manipuri-language fiction feature.

**Cast and Technical Team**

The film features *Bala Hijam Ningthoujam, Leishangthem Tonthoingambi Devi, Angom Pamdamba Singh, Aheibam Chiranjit, Luwang Yumlembam and Ratan Lai.* It also includes several first-time actors from remote villages and relief camps.

The technical and creative team includes Ravi Ranjan Sharma as cinematographer, Meena Longjam as creative director, Amrit Pritam and Debajit Changmai for sound design, Daniel B George for music and Tinni Mitra as editor. Rajni Basumatary serves as executive producer, while Hemam Ricky is the creative producer.

The selection of *Enoong Ngallamdai (Fireflies in the Dark) for KIFF 2026* provides another opportunity for a Manipuri-language film to reach audiences beyond the state, bringing stories rooted in Manipur's experiences to a wider cinematic platform.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
